about.title: About Me
about.subtitle: Professional Background & Investment Insight
about.content: Accounting rigor, fundamental valuation, market trend analysis, knowledge of AI tools, and financial modeling applied to equities and corporate finance. As a Financial Audit Senior at EY (Madrid) specializing in energy sector clients and Private Equity portfolio companies (including Verbund Group and Shell), I hold extensive experience in auditing financial statements under EU-IFRS and Spanish GAAP, fixed assets, CAPEX allocation, financial instruments, revenue recognition (IFRS 15), and due diligence engagements. An Economics graduate from Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, I complement this background with the Master in Financial Markets and Asset Management at IEB and the joint EY-ICADE program, bringing a disciplined capital allocation framework blending Value Investing and CANSLIM.

pos-indra.thesis: Re-rating thesis centered on European defense modernization and aerospace IT digitalization. Structural expansion of European defense procurement, record order backlog backed by multi-year government commitments, and expanding operating leverage with higher EBIT margins.
catalysts: Binding European commitments to lift defense expenditure toward 2% of GDP across NATO members.
Rapid monetization of key defense IT contracts in air traffic control and cyber defense systems.
risks: Project delivery delays in complex multi-nation European defense joint ventures (e.g., FCAS).
State governance and public regulatory scrutiny impacting strategic capital allocation.
pos-indra.lessons_learned: Aligning a powerful secular tailwind (European defense renewal) with clean corporate balance sheets generates over 30% alpha against market benchmarks.

pos-aapl.thesis: Hegemonic brand pricing power, unassailable economic moat rooted in iOS ecosystem switching costs, and high-margin Services revenue expansion delivering >70% gross margins. Substantial share repurchase program funded by predictable annual Free Cash Flow.
catalysts: Major device upgrade supercycle driven by Apple Intelligence embedded across the iOS user base.
Gross margin expansion fueled by higher-margin digital subscriptions and cloud services.
risks: Antitrust scrutiny from the US Department of Justice and EU digital regulation on App Store fees.
Maturity in global smartphone replacement cycles across competitive markets like China.
pos-aapl.lessons_learned: With exceptional quality compounders, staged sales during strong market rallies secure significant gains while preserving exposure to long-term secular innovation.

pos-tsm.thesis: Global foundry monopoly in leading-edge semiconductor nodes (<3nm). Irreplaceable manufacturing partner for Nvidia, Apple, and AMD, commanding exceptional pricing power reflected in 53%+ gross margins and consistent high return on capital.
catalysts: Aggressive enterprise data center deployment of next-generation AI accelerators.
US CHIPS Act co-funding and geographic fab diversification across Arizona and Japan.
risks: Geopolitical cross-strait risk and potential US-China semiconductor export restrictions.
Extremely capital-intensive capex requirements to maintain lithography leadership on 2nm nodes.
pos-tsm.lessons_learned: Targeting the undisputed physical bottleneck of a technological revolution (semiconductor foundry) yields superior risk-adjusted alpha compared to volatile downstream hardware manufacturers.

pos-crdo.thesis: High-growth momentum position applying CANSLIM criteria. Key provider of high-speed SerDes optical connectivity and Active Electrical Cables (AEC) enabling GPU clustering in AI data centers with reduced power dissipation.
catalysts: Tier-1 hyperscale cloud providers replacing optical transceivers with AECs for short-reach server racks.
Consecutive quarterly earnings surprises exceeding consensus expectations (>25% EPS growth).
risks: Customer concentration among a handful of major US hyperscalers.
High stock beta and volatility inherent to mid-cap growth stocks in rapid expansion phases.
pos-crdo.lessons_learned: The CANSLIM framework captures rapid double-digit returns in concise timeframes when accelerating revenue and EPS coincide with heavy institutional volume accumulation.

pos-ko.thesis: Classic Value thesis: inelastic consumer demand, unrivaled global distribution, and demonstrated pricing power to pass through commodity cost inflation without compromising unit volume. Negligible solvency risk and stable dividend yield.
catalysts: Market share gains across emerging markets and favorable product mix shifting to zero-sugar beverages.
Relative valuation outperformance in periods of macro uncertainty and elevated benchmark interest rates.
risks: Packaging input cost spikes (aluminum and PET resin).
Adverse emerging market currency depreciation impacting reported consolidated revenues.
pos-ko.lessons_learned: Defensive equities provide essential portfolio ballast and downside protection, enabling capital preservation and exit with healthy gains when higher-beta growth opportunities emerge.

pos-meta.thesis: Value and CANSLIM combination: re-acceleration of double-digit advertising revenues, disciplined operating cost containment, and AI-driven ad performance delivering operating margin expansion.
catalysts: Increased return on ad spend (ROAS) driven by AI predictive ranking and recommendation systems.
Monetization growth across WhatsApp business messaging and Click-to-Message ad units.
risks: Capital expenditure intensity in custom computing silicon and longer-term metaverse R&D.
Antitrust litigation and user privacy regulatory developments in major jurisdictions.
pos-meta.lessons_learned: In megacap tech, operating margin inflection combined with substantial share repurchases creates favorable asymmetric setups to capture high-probability double-digit returns.

pos-be.thesis: Tactical growth setup in clean energy and on-site solid oxide fuel cell power generation. Technical momentum exhaustion and volume deceleration triggered a disciplined closing of the position.
catalysts: Surging demand for uninterrupted baseload power in AI data centers.
Commercial microgrid supply agreements across industrial clients.
risks: Capital expenditure intensity and fluctuating operating margins.
Commercial adoption lag in hydrogen power infrastructure.
pos-be.lessons_learned: Risk control discipline: detecting volume weakness prompted a tight exit with a minimal loss (-3.21%), validating the principle that cutting small losses quickly safeguards overall portfolio capital.

pos-exi2.thesis: Broad-based mega-cap indexed exposure across the 50 largest global companies. A tactical divestment was executed to reallocate capital into high-conviction individual equity ideas (Indra and Apple).
catalysts: Sustained operating profit expansion across global tech and healthcare titans.
Macro resilience in global enterprise and consumer spending.
risks: Heightened sensitivity to benchmark monetary policy interest rate adjustments.
Opportunity cost relative to high-conviction single-stock opportunities.
pos-exi2.lessons_learned: Agile capital reallocation: exiting with a controlled tactical loss (-12.26%) unlocked liquidity to concentrate the portfolio in leaders with clear double-digit catalysts.

pos-msft.thesis: Enterprise cloud leadership through Azure and integration of generative AI into business workflows. However, elevated valuation multiples and accelerating AI capital expenditure signaled a need for disciplined risk control.
catalysts: Copilot enterprise license monetization across Microsoft 365 commercial seats.
Azure revenue growth outpacing consensus estimates.
risks: Return on invested capital compression from record AI data center capital expenditures.
Technical momentum exhaustion as price action broke below key moving averages.
pos-msft.lessons_learned: CANSLIM risk management rule: honoring the 7-8% stop-loss threshold protected the portfolio against subsequent deeper drawdowns. In professional asset management, promptly recognizing momentum breakdowns preserves capital for higher-conviction ideas.

methodology.title: Investment Methodology
methodology.subtitle: Two Complementary Frameworks
methodology.lead: The investment strategy combines two battle-tested philosophies into a balanced, institutional approach:
methodology.value_title: 1. Value Investing (Fundamental Analysis & Margin of Safety)
methodology.value_subtitle: Strict capital preservation and intrinsic valuation powered by accounting rigor

value_pillars.title: Accounting Scrutiny & Earnings Quality
value_pillars.desc: Thorough audit of the three financial statements under IFRS/GAAP: fixed asset impairment, revenue recognition (IFRS 15), lease liabilities (IFRS 16), and reconciliation of Free Cash Flow against reported EBITDA.

value_pillars.title: Intrinsic Valuation & Discounted Cash Flows (DCF)
value_pillars.desc: Disciplined financial modeling incorporating macroeconomic sensitivity scenarios, normalized mid-cycle operating margins, and conservative discount rates.

value_pillars.title: Durable Competitive Advantages (Economic Moats)
value_pillars.desc: Targeting businesses with sustained high returns on capital employed (ROCE/ROIC > 15%), documented pricing power, and conservative balance sheets (Net Debt / EBITDA < 1.5x).

value_pillars.title: Demanding Margin of Safety
value_pillars.desc: Initiating positions strictly when current market prices offer a substantial discount to estimated intrinsic value, protecting capital against forecasting error.

methodology.canslim_subtitle: Identifying market leaders backed by accelerating earnings and institutional sponsorship

canslim_items.name: Current Quarterly Earnings
canslim_items.desc: Quarterly earnings per share (EPS) acceleration exceeding 20-25% year-over-year, supported by robust revenue growth.

canslim_items.name: Annual Earnings Growth
canslim_items.desc: Compound annual earnings expansion over the past 3 to 5 years, verifying operational scalability.

canslim_items.name: New Product, Service or Highs
canslim_items.desc: Disruptive catalysts: innovative product rollouts, leadership enhancements, or breakouts into new market highs.

canslim_items.name: Supply and Demand
canslim_items.desc: Volume accumulation on upward moves paired with disciplined floating share counts.

canslim_items.name: Leader or Laggard
canslim_items.desc: Selecting the undisputed industry leader demonstrating superior Relative Strength compared to sector peers.

canslim_items.name: Institutional Sponsorship
canslim_items.desc: High-quality institutional accumulation by premier mutual funds and institutional managers.

canslim_items.name: Market Direction & Stop-Loss
canslim_items.desc: Aligning exposure with broad market trends and enforcing an uncompromising 7-8% stop-loss discipline.

research.title: Undergraduate Thesis & Empirical Research
research.subtitle: Econometric Investigation
research.tfg_title: Cryptocurrencies as a Hedge Against Inflation: An Empirical Analysis with Panel Data and Time Series (2017–2024)
research.tfg_meta: Author: Samuel Felipe Marín Muñoz | Advisor: Marta Felis Rota | Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (Faculty of Economics and Business)
research.abstract_text: Empirical econometric study evaluating whether cryptoassets (with focus on Bitcoin) function as a viable hedge and store of value against inflationary shocks and global macro uncertainty, benchmarked against traditional safe havens such as gold and sovereign debt. The paper investigates a multi-variable dataset of 211 countries across 2017–2024 combining World Bank and Statista data.
methodology_items: Fixed Effects Panel Data Regressions controlling for unobserved country and year fixed effects.
Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) estimation and ARIMA time-series models addressing seasonality.
Winsorization of inflation data at 1st and 99th percentiles to eliminate distortion from extreme outliers.
Global sample segmentation by median GDP per capita (High vs. Low GDP nations) and mathematical interaction between Inflation and GDP.
conclusions_items: In high GDP per capita economies, the interaction between inflation and income is positive and statistically significant (p<0.01), showing cryptoassets serve as an inflation hedge under specific macroeconomic conditions.
Technological infrastructure (secure internet servers) and digital access are significantly stronger adoption drivers than inflation rates alone.
In developing economies, cryptocurrencies do not displace gold or sovereign debt as safe havens, but rather act as transactional alternatives where traditional financial infrastructure is absent.
Gold maintains demonstrated long-term empirical superiority as the premier safe haven, whereas cryptoasset volatility and macro sensitivity currently constrain its equivalence.
